Critical review — masque v0.4.0

Source: critical_review_2026-05-17.md

Date: 2026-05-17 (executed under /rpkg end-to-end audit; close-out landed 2026-05-18). Auditor: /rpkg skill driving rpkg_audit.py against masque HEAD b6ff0d8 plus this session’s four mechanical fixes. Verdict: proceed to submission once the Max-controlled publish actions execute (visibility flip + push tags). CRAN gate is green.

1. Summary line

R CMD check --as-cran on a freshly built tarball: 0 errors / 0 warnings / 2 NOTEs. Both NOTEs are environment-only and already justified in cran-comments.md. 403 PASS / 4 SKIP / 0 FAIL under the CRAN-skip subset. Pre-fix invariant score 11/12 → post-fix 12/12 after this session’s three documentation deliverables plus four mechanical fixes.

Cap Limit Current Status

A2.3 — Snapshot tests for verb output recommended not yet present should_fix (v0.4.1 candidate)

Non-base imports (load-bearing, each justified): - cli — user-facing messages (cli_abort, cli_warn, redacted print). - digest — SHA-256 integrity fingerprint on recipe. - MASS — mvrnorm() for Gaussian-copula draws. - Matrix — sparse covariance handling. - S7 — recipe and design_summary class system. - tibble — return type for propose_roles() and friends. - withr — RNG hygiene (local_preserve_seed, with_seed).

The A2b cap is exceeded by two. Trimming options for v0.4.1: inline mvrnorm via chol(Σ) %*% rnorm(n) to drop MASS; the rest are load-bearing. Not a CRAN blocker.

6. Findings to act on (not in this branch)

6.1 Pre-existing local-suite regression (v0.4.1 candidate)

devtools::test() against Max’s local MET fixtures shows two ERRORs that are invisible to R CMD check --as-cran because the tests are skip_on_cran():

  • tests/testthat/test-mask-end-to-end.R:97 — “mask() runs end-to-end on MET tab_04”
  • tests/testthat/test-mask-roundtrip-integration.R:88 — “Round-trip on MET tab_04”

Both abort with:

Error in `roles_validate(roles, df)`:
  Multiple columns (3) flagged as "treatment": Genotype, ACPC, and M_WEATHER.
  v0.2 supports at most one treatment column.
  Joint-treatment masking is deferred to v0.3.

Root cause: v0.3.0 made propose_roles(detect = TRUE) the default behaviour; on the MET fixture, design-detection legitimately labels three columns as treatment-like. The v0.2-era single-treatment guard in roles_validate() was not updated to match. The error message itself still talks about “v0.2” and “deferred to v0.3”, which is now stale.

Resolution options (Max’s call):

  1. Tighten the two integration tests to call propose_roles(df, detect = FALSE) so they preserve v0.2 semantics end-to-end. Cleanest if detect = TRUE is the intended user-facing default for mask().
  2. Relax roles_validate() to accept multiple treatments and route them through the existing collaborate-mode aliasing pipeline. Larger change; needs a design pass on what “joint-treatment masking” should actually do.
  3. Document the constraint as known and gate detect-on-multiple-treatment datasets with a clearer message that recommends explicitly editing the roles tibble before calling mask().

Not a CRAN blocker; CRAN never sees these tests. Worth a v0.4.1 release once Max picks an option.

6.2 Audit-emitted WARNs on jitter tests (expected)

Three testthat WARN entries on tests/testthat/test-synthesise_numeric_jitter.R (lines 76, 120, 138) come from audit_mask() flagging HIGH leakage on the Rep column when collaborate mode jitters integer outcomes. The tests pass; the warnings are the audit doing its job. No action.

6.3 Stale roles_validate() error message

The error string in section 6.1 still references “v0.2” and “deferred to v0.3”, which is now factually wrong (we are on v0.4.0). Whichever resolution is taken for 6.1, refresh the message wording.

  • Trim Imports to satisfy A2b cap (MASS is the obvious drop; the other six are load-bearing).
  • Snapshot tests via expect_snapshot() for verb output and key error messages (A2.3).
  • covr + Codecov configuration (F8).
  • Fix items in section 6.

None of these block CRAN submission of v0.4.0.

8. False positives cleared

The audit driver’s credential-leak scan flagged two strings; both verified safe:

  • R/propose_roles.R:186 — string literal inside a PII-pattern regex used by propose_roles() itself to detect potential PII columns for the user. Legitimate.
  • .github/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml:33 — ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }} is the standard GitHub Actions idiom and is never expanded into the repository. Legitimate.
